posts.cooked: I minted it with Wraith and Chrono-Ranger at 8 HP, Haka at 12, and Bunker and Legacy at 13. I honestly forgot that Gloomweaver had a flip side! Vast Following brought out two killed relics while his third one was still out, and then there I was, seeing his flip side in action on the app for the first time ever in over 500 hours of play. posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
Almost max HP. 27,26,28,30,27. Here's my writeup from the playtest boards:

Enjoyed this one. First turn relic that potentially does a ton of damage was alarming. I decided to focus on DR so used the Stun Bolt. I hadn't actually noticed the game was Advanced until that attack unexpectedly did no damage! Then I panicked a bit more when the second relic came out, but soon twigged that going after the relics was the way to win this game and Take Down/Eyepiece would be my friends.

I've never left the Atlantean Throne Room in play before! It's DR was great against the relic. Later I had a lovely combination of Main Computer Room giving me card draw while Take Down prevented extra villain plays and then Fixed Point kept the Take Down around another round.

By the late game it was clear the well set up heroes had everything easily under control and I coasted to a nearly full HP victory, but it was pretty exciting in the beginning and the desire to make sure I got mint kept me on the edge of my seat even in the mid game.

 

Used Ultimate Target on GloomWeaver, despite not actually intending to attack GloomWeaver, in order to get the extra power users throughout the game. Put By Any Means on the relics to focus fire one each one in turn.

posts.cooked:
Is everyone getting the same setups?  I minted this one pretty easily; the only thing I can figure is that I made optimal plays by accident.  I'm seeing other people using Eyepiece - I never got Eyepiece.

The key for me was probably being aggressive and playing two early Take Downs in a row after I'd whacked the first relic and was working on the remainig two.  That, plus the three relics were all served up pretty early.  I figured that the Take Downs and Wraiths environment scouting ability meant that I was on a short clock until Gloomy's Vast Following came up.  As it turned out, the turn I killed the third relic, I had Wraith scout the environment deck just in case and she trashed the Main Computer Room that plays the top card of the villain deck - I guess we'll never know if that woulda shuffed in the three dead relics. (edit - nevermind) Legacy was the MVP as usual.  Wraith and Chrono did most of the heavy lifting on DPS, Haka threw in a Rampage and an Elbow Smash, Bunker stalled the environment deck for a turn and exploded the first wave of zombies.  It seemed like it went really smooth, but apparently I could've been >.< close to having my win snatched away with Vast Following?

posts.name: ClericalError
posts.cooked:
Wow. Reading all these comments and it doesn't look like anybody else used the same strategy I used. (See pic attached for effectiveness)

http://oi67.tinypic.com/i78weq.jpg

 

Basically, use Chrono-Ranger and Wraith's "Search for Equipment" cards to grab a Neuro-Toxin Dart Thrower and two Stun Bolts. Throw out the damage reduction items like Plating, Recharge Mode, Fortitude and Ta' Moko.

These items combo extremely well with Atlantean Throne Room so the relics effectively do nothing. You can skip pretty much everything late game and Gloomweaver will do literally zero damage. Just throw out a Rampage if the Zombies are a problem.

 

I loved this one! really showcasing how different strengths of these characters can be used to secure victory in different ways. MINT.

posts.name: schadkehnfreude
posts.cooked:
Hrm - I initially also tried using multiple stun bolts from Wraith on the relics but then found out (since I can't read good) that the relics don't do damage, they make *Gloomweaver* do damage - and I can't use stun bolts on Gloomweaver since he's immune to projectile damage.  So I just said eff it and burned down the relics.   That said, it's still not a bad idea at all to stack Neuro-Toxin Darts along with the Atlantean Throne Room and damage resisting ongoings - that is a safer strategy for not getting blindsided by Vast Following or the environment.

Other interesting thing - between getting Rook City Wraith and 3x Enduring Intercession, I initially interpreted that as a signal that my strategy should be to manipulate the environment deck to win the game but I shortly abandoned that notion and just spammed grenades to stall the env deck instead.
